newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic profits bolstered by ICD sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic profits bolstered by ICD sales growth.

text.p: Medtronic Inc., the largest U.S. manufacturer of medical devices, Tuesday reported solidly higher profits for the quarter ended Aug. 1, boosted by strong growth in sales of implantable defibrillators, or ICDs.
The small electronic devices are implanted in the body and wired to the heart to keep it from beating too fast.

Medtronic posted first-quarter earnings of $146 million, or 63 cents per share, topping the First Call consensus estimate by 1 cent per share. In the same period last year Medtronic earned $127.4 million, or 53 cents per share.
Net sales rose to $646.3 million from $600.8 million.

"Heavy expenditures on research and development over a number of years have leveraged our core competencies into new therapeutic devices that are now winning market acceptance," said Chairman William George.
Performance in Medtronic's key pacing business benefited from a 37.2 percent unit-sales increase in sales of ICDs.
Unit volumes of pacemakers -- similar to ICDs but designed to keep the heart from beating too slowly -- grew in the mid-single-digit range, Medtronic said.
Sales in the company's vascular business posted a quarterly growth rate in the high teens, as sales of coronary stents grew nearly 50 percent on a constant-currency basis.
Neurological sales rose more than 30 percent on a constant currency basis, the company said. Cardiac surgery revenues rose modestly.
Medtronic's stock rose $3.81 to $91.44 on the New York Stock Exchange.
